title: Choose tense and voice for science
objective: Use the present for a general fact and the past for a completed action.

slides.title: Choose time, then focus
body: For general facts, use the present: “Roots take in water.”
For a completed class action, use the past. Put the receiver first if you want a passive sentence.

slides.title: Move the focus to the object
body: The action and time stay the same. Were agrees with the plural subject leaves.

slides.title: Read the first case together
body: Class notes: Leaves use sunlight. Yesterday, students counted leaves on three branches.

slides.title: Try it with a partner
body: Copy the general fact. Name its tense.
Copy the completed action. Name its tense.
Find the sentence that is generally true.

slides.title: Try a new case
body: Class notes: Birds lay eggs. Yesterday, students counted birds in three trees.

slides.title: Work on your own
body: Copy the general fact. Name its tense.
Copy the completed action. Name its tense.
Rewrite the completed action in the passive voice.

slides.title: Read your passive sentence
body: Point to the receiver, was or were, and the past participle. Can your partner tell that the action is complete?
